practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses an explicit timeout annotation (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related assertion; therefore a performance concern is present and handled.
The method name 'test8' is generic and does not convey the scenario or expected result; it does not follow descriptive naming patterns like method_condition_expectedResult.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: Signs of test-generation tooling are present: class uses EvoRunner/EvoRunnerParameters and the test method has an autogenerated-style name 'test8', indicating heavy code generation artifacts rather than minimal hand-written tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test appears to be a single quick check with no Given-When-Then comments, BDD-style naming, or coverage of multiple scenarios, suggesting it was written post-implementation rather than following a prioritized design approach.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API methods (Grafo constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices) and does not rely on reflection or private/internal state, indicating behavior-focused testing.

Assertions lack descriptive failure messages; they use assertNotSame and assertEquals without messages, and only a small set of properties are asserted—improving messages and specificity would aid diagnosability.
practices_evaluation.original_code:
assertNotSame(grafo1, grafo0);
assertEquals(100, grafo0.numVertices());
practices_evaluation.improved_code:
assertNotSame("Transpose must return a different Grafo instance", grafo1, grafo0);
assertEquals("Original graph should have 100 vertices", 100, grafo0.numVertices());

practices_evaluation.justification: Class-level Javadoc documents requirement traceability and notes; the test itself is concise and does not contain excessive or misleading comments.
The test uses deterministic operations (no Random, no current time, and no Thread.sleep) and relies solely on local state; no non-deterministic constructs are present in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local Grafo instances and does not persist data, modify static variables, or leave open resources; no cleanup is required for visible actions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization for selective execution.
